### fisher-kpp-speed - BENCHMARK-LINKED
- content sha256 `da1f743727e4d1359a0a9c450e035962f1f3a24d49e04a68b78cb569b71d48d7` (canonical JSON of record fields); retrieved 2026-10-31T15:03:21Z; type model-theorem
- Point 1 (headline, as in record): An advantageous allele spreading through a continuous population advances as a travelling wave whose speed is set by the selection coefficient and the diffusion (dispersal) rate.
- Point 2 (source, as in record): Ronald A. Fisher (1937) The wave of advance of advantageous genes
- Point 7 (math, as in record): `u_t = D u_{xx} + s u(1-u); travelling waves u(x-ct) exist iff c \ge c^* = 2\sqrt{sD}; compactly supported initial data spread at asymptotic speed c^*`
- Evidence: scopedesk/bench/v1_2/key.jsonl (family fisher_kpp_speed, 16 items); scopedesk/bench/v1_2/key_verification.json (independent finite-difference front speeds: logistic ~2, pushed cubic alpha=10/3: 2.062 vs analytic 2.066; Allee 0.2817 vs 0.2828)
- Scope finding: The record specifies logistic growth and says Allee effects change the speed; the bench compares it with alternative reaction terms (strong Allee; u(1-u)(1+alpha u), where 2*sqrt(sD) holds iff alpha<=2). These are out-of-model comparisons, not a missing condition and not an erroneous theorem.
- Does NOT establish: Declared reaction terms on the line with wide initial data; exact travelling-profile residuals and PDE speeds do not prove minimal-speed selection or a PDE existence theorem (cited, not reproved).

### hamilton-rule - BENCHMARK-LINKED
- content sha256 `86130c5e0ed4e508645b7880e357077d488123603a346dd92622f644c4782d71` (canonical JSON of record fields); retrieved 2026-10-31T15:03:21Z; type model-theorem
- Point 1 (headline, as in record): A gene for social behaviour increases in frequency when the benefit to the recipient, weighted by genetic relatedness, exceeds the cost to the actor.
- Point 2 (source, as in record): W. D. Hamilton (1964) The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I
- Point 7 (math, as in record): `\Delta \bar{p} > 0 \iff r b - c > 0, with r, b, c defined as regression coefficients (Queller form via the Price equation)`
- Evidence: scopedesk/bench/v1_2/key.jsonl (family hamilton_rule_form, 16 items); lean_price/Price.lean (queller, hamilton_form; README with prior-art correction; commit e776030); experiments/price_probe/ on work/codex-api (Codex's own Price/Hamilton probe; separate artifact)
- Scope finding: The record defines b, c, r as REGRESSION coefficients and distinguishes this from the original additive assumptions. Our compiled corollary: sign(Cov(w,z)) = sign(r*b - c) under exact linearity in own and partner genotype with an orthogonal residual. A synergy witness with FIXED ADDITIVE payoff coefficients is not a counterexample to the regression identity; it illustrates why the additive reading differs.
- Does NOT establish: No defect in this record and no complete empirical test. The corollary is conditional (sufficient covariance/orthogonality conditions; sign agreement can also occur outside them, so 'exactly when' was overstated in v0). Haploid pairing model with a stated kernel. Price/Queller algebra duplicates existing formalization in part (atlas-lean has Price).
- Codex-reviewed: Codex v0 review (planning/rethink/CODEX-SCORECARD-V0-REVIEW.md @ 4fe9fb7, non-blinded): record transcription (hash + copied fields) passes; corrected description below is the one Codex approved. ### kimura-fixation-probability - BENCHMARK-LINKED
- content sha256 `859527bc0b704a138bbd5509f70874fba40ea23ef2a2b66eb03567d554f6ce9f` (canonical JSON of record fields); retrieved 2026-10-31T15:03:22Z; type model-theorem
- Point 1 (headline, as in record): The probability that a mutant allele eventually fixes in a finite population depends on its initial frequency, its selective advantage and the effective population size, and equals its initial frequency when it is neutral.
- Point 2 (source, as in record): Motoo Kimura (1962) On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population
- Point 7 (math, as in record): `u(p) = \frac{1-e^{-4N_e s p}}{1-e^{-4N_e s}}; neutral limit u(p) = p, so a new mutant fixes with probability 1/(2N)`
- Evidence: scopedesk/bench/v1_2/key.jsonl (family kimura_regime, 16 items); scopedesk/bench/v1_2/key_verification.json (power-iteration of the exact haploid Wright-Fisher chain)
- Scope finding: The record states a diffusion approximation (diploid convention). The bench uses a finite HAPLOID Wright-Fisher chain: in a neutral finite chain eventual fixation equals initial frequency EXACTLY (1/N for one copy of N haploid copies; 1/(2N) for N diploid individuals); using that neutral value under nonzero selection is an approximation, and the diffusion formula can be off at small N and large s (bench witnesses, 10% tolerance).
- Does NOT establish: The 10% tolerance is a benchmark choice, not a universal validity boundary; ploidy mapping between the chain and the record is not validated; atlas-lean (MathlibExt/Biology/PopulationGenetics/Diffusion/KimuraFixationProcess.lean) formalizes related material that we did not compare.
- Codex-reviewed: Codex v0 review (planning/rethink/CODEX-SCORECARD-V0-REVIEW.md @ 4fe9fb7, non-blinded): record transcription (hash + copied fields) passes; corrected description below is the one Codex approved. ### turing-ddi - BENCHMARK-LINKED
- content sha256 `6f278b74291bc5eb7d85862b30a0ed669ad9a70278742d5b13e8b99e658cb9a8` (canonical JSON of record fields); retrieved 2026-10-31T15:03:24Z; type model-theorem
- Point 1 (headline, as in record): A homogeneous steady state of two reacting chemicals that is stable without diffusion can become unstable to spatial perturbations when the chemicals diffuse at different rates, spontaneously producing a pattern.
- Point 2 (source, as in record): Alan Turing (1952) The chemical basis of morphogenesis
- Point 7 (math, as in record): `u_t = f(u,v) + D_u \nabla^2 u, v_t = g(u,v) + D_v \nabla^2 v; with tr J < 0 and det J > 0, instability at some wavenumber k iff D_v f_u + D_u g_v > 2\sqrt{D_u D_v \det J}, which requires D_u \ne D_v`
- Evidence: scopedesk/bench/v1_2/key.jsonl (families turing_finite_domain 21 items, turing_2d_rectangle 15); turing_scope/examples/short_L_pi.json (J=[[1,-2],[2,-3]], Du=1, Dv=10: continuum band 1/5<q<1/2 non-empty, no admissible Neumann mode at L=pi; a mode appears at L=2pi); turing_scope/lean/Audit.lean (+ docs/turing-scope.md): integer-model determinant/trace and mode-tail algebra, mutants; scopedesk/bench/audit/oracle_layer_audit_v1_2.json (NCA oracle 50/50 incl. these families)
- Scope finding: The record gives a continuum instability criterion on a fixed domain without specifying the admissible spectrum; the witness shows that the determinant at an ACTUAL admissible mode is the right target, and that mode sets differ between Neumann, Dirichlet and periodic boundaries and between 1-D and 2-D domains.
- Does NOT establish: Linear stability of a DECLARED two-species Jacobian only; no full PDE theorem, no nonlinear-pattern conclusion, no biology, no historical novelty (finite-domain mode quantisation is classical).

- Point 1 (headline, as in record): The spacing of a Turing pattern at onset is set by the reaction rates and diffusivities, not by the size of the tissue, so changing these parameters predictably changes the number of repeated elements.

- Does NOT establish: Keeps three things distinct: the onset formula, the linear fastest mode, and a nonlinear selected pattern (the NCA study found the latter often differs from the linear prediction). The 10% tolerance and the 'largest real part' convention are ours.

- Point 1 (headline, as in record): When the cost of injury exceeds the value of the contested resource, the stable outcome is a mixture in which animals escalate with probability equal to the ratio of resource value to injury cost.
- Point 2 (source, as in record): John Maynard Smith (1982) Evolution and the Theory of Games
- Point 7 (math, as in record): `payoffs E(H,H) = (V-C)/2, E(H,D) = V, E(D,H) = 0, E(D,D) = V/2; for C > V the unique ESS plays Hawk with probability p^* = V/C`

- Does NOT establish: The matrix and C>V are in the record; the checked algebra (E(p*,q)-E(q,q)=(C/2)(p*-q)^2>0) concerns the symmetric two-strategy model, with the physical-payoff condition 0<V<C retained. Not validation in animal populations, finite populations or asymmetric contests.

### fisher-ftns - RELATED FORMAL LEMMA, TARGET NOT ESTABLISHED
- content sha256 `d7832308474c4a0e87d984b0764f7b7d7c928a2d4509368f7cf34e0f028a97fe` (canonical JSON of record fields); retrieved 2026-10-31T15:03:20Z; type model-theorem
- Point 1 (headline, as in record): The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.
- Point 2 (source, as in record): Ronald A. Fisher (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection
- Point 7 (math, as in record): `\Delta_{NS}\bar{w} = V_A(w)/\bar{w} (discrete generations); \left.\frac{d\bar{m}}{dt}\right|_{NS} = V_A(m) for Malthusian fitness m`
- Evidence: lean_price/Price.lean (Price identity; the z=w case gives Var(w) but is not stated as a separate theorem); facebookresearch/atlas-lean MathlibExt/Biology/PopulationGenetics/Selection.lean (Price and a haploid total-variance selection identity; its docs exclude the diploid additive-genetic statement) - existing work, not ours; experiments/price_probe/ on work/codex-api (Codex: fitness_selection is total-variance selection, NOT additive-genetic Fisher FTNS)
- Does NOT establish: A Price identity and a total-fitness-variance selection identity do NOT establish additive genetic variance or Fisher's partial-change target; the record already states those qualifications. Do not count this as a successful theorem or a faithful target attempt without a target/run receipt; the genetic projection and fixed-average-effect semantics must be frozen before any prover run.
- Codex-reviewed: Codex v0 review: target not established; related formal artifact available (CODEX-SCORECARD-V0-REVIEW.md @ 4fe9fb7). Transcription passes.

- Does NOT establish: An empirical claim about the world can have formalizable estimators, so it is NOT 'not formalizable'; but a model proof alone cannot settle it. It needs a specified population, estimator, denominator conditions and data.
